rows.text: The impulse to change Bitcoin’s rules merely to prevent others from using Bitcoin in ways you disapprove of is statist and alien to a community rooted in liberty, property rights, free markets, natural law, and Austrian economics. BIP 110 would impose monetary purity by fiat.

A new type of "high-level programming language" that seems really worth trying to make, is a language that gets compiled to Lean (or HOL, or...) that is specifically about making it as friendly as possible for a human to read definitions and theorems.

Not the proofs - as all that matters with proofs is that the proofs are correct - just the definitions and theorems.

The intended use case is that AI outputs a blob of proofs, and you're trying to make it as easy as possible for anyone reading the output to understand what the actual precise claims are that have been proven

Capitalism is a powerful force for good. It benefits everyone, especially those who lean in and help build the future.

But it’s under attack (again). Wealth taxes, price controls, government-run grocery stores, asset seizures. Fear is being used as a political lever and an excuse for control. I’ve seen this play out before, it leads nowhere good.

I lived in Buenos Aires in 2008 when the Argentine government seized $30B in private pensions to ‘protect’ citizens from the financial crisis. Then they froze access to the dollar and nationalized companies. Within a decade, inflation was over 50%. The elites had miraculously moved their money, leaving regular people to take the financial hit.

Politicians are selling collectivism out of the same playbook used by Argentina, Venezuela, and the former Soviet Union: promise protection, concentrate power, tighten the fist. And the costs fall on the poorest people in society who are unable to protect themselves.

Capitalism isn't perfect. But it’s far better than every alternative that’s been tried. Millions of people making independent decisions, with the free market rewarding the best ideas, will out-build any central planner.

科技 ETF 单月流出接近 90 亿美元，美股资金轮动已经越来越明显

前面我写过，美国科技板块基金曾经在一周内流入超过 200 亿美元，随后又迅速转为 150 亿美元净流出。高盛 Prime Book 的数据也显示，对冲基金对美国信息科技板块的卖出一度达到 2016 年以来最极端的水平。

最新一个月，科技板块 ETF 净流出接近 90 亿美元，远远超过其他行业。金融板块获得约 20 亿美元净流入，医疗、公用事业、工业和必需消费也有小幅资金进入。

这说明过去几年资金最集中、估值最高、涨幅最大的科技和 AI 交易，已经开始被系统性减仓。撤出的资金正在流向金融、医疗、公用事业和工业等估值相对较低、现金流更稳定、前期涨幅较小的板块。

不过虽然金融板块拿到了最多资金，但仍远低于科技板块接近 90 亿美元的流出。其他行业的流入加在一起，也没有完全接住科技板块撤出的资金。还有相当一部分资金可能转向现金、债券或者其他资产，市场整体的风险偏好正在下降。

但有趣的是最近明显能看到有部分的资金流入到了 Bitcoin 中。

这和前面机构、对冲基金和散户的数据可以连起来看。机构已经在降低科技股敞口，散户近一个月净买入也降到约 130 亿美元，是 2020 年以来最低水平。与此同时，散户总成交额仍然接近 5,000 亿美元，每 100 美元成交只能形成约 2.6 美元净买入，交易依然活跃，真正留下来的增量资金却越来越少。

最大的风险在于，科技股在标普 500 和纳斯达克中的权重太高。如果是更多的资金在从科技股撤出的话，标普500 和纳指很有可能也会出现回撤。
